23 A transverse progressive wave on a string has a wavelength of 12 cm and an amplitude of 1.5 cm.
The speed of the wave on the string is 48 cm s–1.
What is the distance travelled by a point on the string in a time of 2.0 s?
A
12 cm
B
24 cm
C
48 cm
D
96 cm

hints: Notice the question asks for the path of a point on the string, which vibrates up and down with amplitude $1.5\text{ cm}$, not the forward distance moved by the wave pattern.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 48\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ and $\lambda = 12\text{ cm}$ to find the frequency and then the period $T$ of one oscillation of the point.
Count how many periods fit in $2.0\text{ s}$ and multiply by the distance travelled in one full cycle, which is $4$ times the amplitude.
walkthrough: Find the oscillation period of a point. The wave equation is $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda = 48/12 = 4.0\text{ Hz}$. Hence $T = 1/f = 0.25\text{ s}$.
Find the number of oscillations in the given time. $N = t/T = 2.0/0.25 = 8.0$ full cycles.
Find the path in one cycle. A point moves from centre to peak to centre to trough to centre, so distance per cycle $= 4A = 4 \times 1.5\text{ cm} = 6.0\text{ cm}$.
Multiply to get the total path: $s = N \times 4A = 8 \times 6.0\text{ cm} = 48\text{ cm}$, with units of length as required.

A.explanation: This is only $2$ amplitudes. A point travels $4$ amplitudes in every full oscillation, and many oscillations occur in $2.0\text{ s}$.

B.explanation: This is $4$ amplitudes or one full oscillation. The $2.0\text{ s}$ time contains $8$ full periods, so the distance is much larger.

C.explanation: With period $0.25\text{ s}$ there are $8$ oscillations in $2.0\text{ s}$, each of path $4 \times 1.5\text{ cm} = 6.0\text{ cm}$, giving $48\text{ cm}$.

D.explanation: This confuses the wave travel distance $48 \times 2.0 = 96\text{ cm}$ with the oscillation path of a single point on the string.
